summary: Kensuke Nedachi works in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1975 to 1984 and later served there as a professor from circa 2004 to 2022.
Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He has served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College.

Kenyu Mitomo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley under teachers including Kyoko Motai, Akira Hirakawa, Ensho Kanakura, and Seiren Matsunami. He held positions at Rissho University, UC Berkeley, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Otani University.

Kevin A. Vose specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his BA from Bates College and his PhD from the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins, also studying under Ngawang Jinpa.

Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisors Chun-fang Yu, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.
Khakyab Dorje was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé from circa 1886 to 1899 and under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo from circa 1886 to 1892.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He has served as a fellow and trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies and as a professor at International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued his traditional studies under Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Thrangu Monastery, served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery, and directed the Karma Shri Nalanda Institute.

Khenpo Appey was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Khenpo Dragyab Lodro. He held posts at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as director of Sakya College from 1972 to 1985.
Khenpo Dazer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima. He served as a teacher at Dzogchen Monastery and at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1959.

Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Thrangu Monastery. He taught at Rumtek Monastery in 1959 and served as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra beginning in 1978.
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teachers Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.

Khenpo Palden Sherab was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries, later serving as chair of the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from circa 1967 to 1984.
Khenpo Shenga was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and founded Dzongsar Monastery.

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche and the 14th Dalai Lama. He founded Nyingmapa Wishfulfilling Center and taught at Tokyo, Kyoto, and Virginia universities.

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Khenpo Shenga, Rasvir Das, and Dev Narayan Tripathi. He taught at Men-Tsee-Khang.

Kichinosuke Ito was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1906 to 1909. He held academic posts at Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo as a professor, and Chuo University.
Kim Gutschow specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at Harvard University from circa 1991 to 1998 and has taught at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She held academic posts at the University of Leeds from circa 1983 to 2012 and at Lancaster University beginning around 2012.
